description: KeyCortexController commands are attributed to the authenticated member (R0-09-ID-HARDEN review R09-ST-4 and CR-3; R0-34b review ST-3). Every KeyCortexController handler that hands a user to a service takes it from @CurrentUser() (the principal AuthGuard admitted) through requestActorId; a body or query userId naming someone else is IGNORED (pinned: not refused; the DTOs keep it as an optional string), and with no authenticated user the handler answers 401 instead of running as 'system', 'key_user' or nobody. The KEY settings adapter applies IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner (owner ruling D-11) on the command's actor with its User role before settings.update_business_profile and settings.update_branding: a STAFF or ADMIN (settings:write) command answers 200 with the connector failure shape (result.success false, 'Only the business owner can edit the business profile') and leaves the Business row byte-identical; the OWNER membership, the Business.ownerId owner and SUPER_ADMIN succeed. Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/key-cortex-actor-binding.integration.test.ts src/modules/key-cortex/adapters/settings-adapter.service.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex.controller.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-09c-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/key-cortex-actor-binding.json --report .proof/r0-09c-vitest.json. RED-BEFORE (claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb at a230d7fc, tests-first commit 3a6b4076): the real-database suite failed 15 of 22 (execute with body userId=OWNER ran the command as the OWNER; execute with no userId ran as 'system'; the natural-language path parsed and built for the body user; POST query routed its command with userId undefined; rollback named 'system'; batch named the body user for every command; STAFF and ADMIN settings.update_business_profile / update_branding succeeded and changed the row; conscious/stream, conscious/chat and POST sessions wrote CortexSession rows for the outsider named in the request; chat, chat/stream and stream handed the reasoning engine the request user, stream 'key_user' when none; GET sessions?userId=OWNER listed the OWNER's session to a STAFF member; feedback recorded the outsider). The settings-adapter spec failed 9 of 21 and the controller spec 9 of 19. Cases without RED-BEFORE passed before the fix and are controls (AuthGuard 401, BusinessGuard 403 for a member of another business, OWNER and SUPER_ADMIN writes, delegation of the other settings actions). After the red run, three execute cases were changed from an exact list of routed commands to the command plus at most its compensating revert_<action> (the executor's rollbackOnFailure attempt, which runs only once the adapter refuses), every one still for the STAFF member. SCOPE LIMIT (review ST-5 / CR-2): the actor binding holds within KeyCortexController and the settings adapter, not for every KEY command. KEY plans still take a body userId: KeyCortexGoalsController (POST plans, goals/:id/plans) hands the planner dto.userId, the planner builds each step as plan.userId ?? 'key_cortex', and POST plans/:id/execute takes no actor, so a STAFF member naming the OWNER still runs plan steps as the OWNER. The fix is in key-cortex-goals.controller.ts and key-cortex-planner.service.ts, outside this write set, recorded as an it.todo in the real-database suite; until it lands this manifest is not evidence that every KEY command acts for the authenticated member. REVIEW REPAIRS (pkt/R0-09c-KEY-ACTOR-BINDING-repair on 056e9e8d): ST-1..ST-4, a session is the member's who opened it: GET/PATCH/DELETE sessions/:id, GET messages (with or without sessionId), POST chat, GET chat/stream, GET stream, POST conscious/chat, GET conscious/stream, POST feedback and POST personalities/switch hand the session services only one of the authenticated user's own sessions in the guard-checked tenant (KeyCortexController.ownSession): another tenant's session, cached or not, and another member's session are not found (an error event once an SSE stream is committed), GET messages with no sessionId reads the caller's own newest session, and an id naming no session still starts a new session (or records a new feedback row) for the caller. CR-1, settings.remove_team_member and update_role refuse a command whose parameters.userId is not a non-empty string before any lookup, so the executor compensation for a failed add_team_member (remove_team_member with the add's {email, role}) and a command with no target no longer delete or re-role whichever membership Postgres reads first. ST-6, settings.configure_integration applies ModuleScopeGuard's rule on the command actor (connect at write or above from the explicit scope map or else the role defaults; SUPER_ADMIN passes), so STAFF, an ADMIN granted settings:write and an OWNER without a connect grant are refused, as on the HTTP connections routes. RED-BEFORE the repair (the repair tests on 056e9e8d): the real-database suite failed 9 of 34 (every new RED-BEFORE case; in that run the CR-1 compensation deleted a membership, so the ST-6 case was re-run alone on 056e9e8d and failed on the assertion itself, STAFF disconnect success true), the controller spec 5 of 25 (the four new RED-BEFORE cases and the strengthened messages case, which now asserts listSessions(businessId, actor)), and the settings-adapter spec 4 of 27; the positive controls passed. allowAdditionalCases is true only because the real-database suite carries two it.todo hand-offs outside this write set (ST-5 / CR-2 above, and ST-7: KeyCortexExecutorService.logExecution writes fields AiExecutionLog does not have, so no ai_execution_logs row records the actor); requireReportSuccess keeps every reported case binding.
notes: Out of scope, left to V1-03-KEY-CORTEX-PRINCIPAL (blocked on D-17): autonomy-profile write authority (who may change tiers and the kill switch: PATCH autonomy-profile is still membership-only) and the autonomy orchestrator's use of proposedBy beyond receiving the authenticated id (the suite's orchestrator is a recording stand-in).

GET sessions lists the authenticated user's own sessions (it listed every session of the business when no ?userId was sent, or the named user's). The review repair closes the rest of within-tenant session privacy on this controller: GET messages with no sessionId reads the caller's own newest session, and every handler that takes a session id refuses another member's session (KeyCortexController.ownSession). Sessions written before R0-09c under userId 'system' or 'key_user' are reachable by nobody through these routes.

Open, outside this write set, recorded as it.todo in the real-database suite: review ST-5 / CR-2, KeyCortexGoalsController createPlanFromGoal and createPlanFromCommand hand the planner dto.userId, the planner's buildCommand runs every step as plan.userId ?? 'key_cortex', and POST plans/:id/execute takes no actor, so a spoofed actor still reaches the settings adapter through KEY plans; review ST-7, KeyCortexExecutorService.logExecution writes fields AiExecutionLog does not have (traceId, parameters, commandJson, ...), so every execute logs 'Failed to persist audit log' and no ai_execution_logs row is written (observed in this suite).

POST query routes its 'query' name to the module adapter as a command like any other (settings.update_business_profile included); it now names the authenticated actor, so the owner rule applies there too.

KeyCortexLearningService.recordFeedback still matches the cognition memory it rewrites by sessionId alone (key-cortex-learning.service.ts, outside this write set). The controller now refuses feedback on a session that is not the caller's own, which covers conversation sessions; a memory keyed by an id that is not a CortexSession (the tool registry can key outcomes by a correlation id) is not covered by that check.
